headline: Westfield Quarry gets $680,000 state grant to shift more stone shipments to rail
dek: MassDOT says the project could add about 1,700 railcars a year, remove an estimated 5,950 truck trips from area roads and help retain 21 jobs.
body: A Westfield quarry will receive $680,000 from Massachusetts to rebuild and expand an industrial rail siding, a project state transportation officials say could move more stone by train and reduce truck traffic on area roads. The grant to John S. Lane & Son Inc., a Peckham Industries company, was announced Oct. 1 by the Massachusetts Department of Transportation. The work is planned at the Westfield Quarry, where the company already has rail access but needs larger siding capacity for expanded freight operations.

MassDOT estimates the upgraded siding could support about 1,700 additional railcars each year. The agency also estimates that the shift from trucks to rail would eliminate roughly 5,950 truck trips annually and help retain 21 jobs. Those figures are projections tied to the planned project, not a record of traffic reductions or jobs already created. The state announcement does not provide a construction start date, a completion date or a final total project cost.

The announcement matters locally because quarry products are heavy and move through the region’s existing road and rail network. Each train shipment can replace multiple truck movements, although the exact number depends on the material, the railcar and the delivery route. MassDOT says the project is expected to improve freight efficiency, reduce roadway congestion and emissions, and support continued employment at the quarry. It describes the benefit as a transportation and economic-development investment, not simply a grant to expand a private facility.

The money comes through the Industrial Rail Access Program, a competitive state-funded public-private partnership administered by MassDOT. The program is intended for companies investing in rail infrastructure that increases use of the freight network, improves distribution efficiency and helps retain or grow industrial activity. Its rules require recipients to provide matching funds equal to at least 20% of eligible project costs. The [program overview](https://www.mass.gov/industrial-rail-access-program) says applications are reviewed quarterly on a rolling basis.

Westfield’s freight connections give the grant a broader regional context. The Pioneer Valley Railroad is a short-line carrier serving the Westfield area, and [The Westfield News reported in 2019](https://thewestfieldnews.com/pioneer-valley-railroad-gives-unique-experience/) that it handled stone, lumber, steel and other products between Westfield and Holyoke. That article described the railroad as moving thousands of cars annually and explained that a railcar can carry the equivalent of several truckloads. The older account provides background on the local network; it does not measure the future Westfield Quarry project or establish how the new siding will be operated.

MassDOT identified the quarry as a John S. Lane & Son operation, and a [CSX directory of aggregate producers](https://www.csx.com/index.cfm/customers/commodities/minerals/aggregates-and-other-specialty-stone/resources/ballast-producers/) lists Westfield Quarry at 311 East Mountain Road. Those records establish the facility’s location and operator, while MassDOT’s release identifies the siding work and its expected benefits. Neither source describes changes to public road design, truck bans or a new rail line through residential neighborhoods.

The next step is project implementation: rebuilding and expanding the existing siding, securing the required private match and coordinating the work with the freight railroad and quarry operations. The public announcement leaves open how long construction will take and when the added rail capacity will begin carrying shipments. For Westfield and surrounding communities, the measurable test will be whether the project reaches the projected railcar volume, reduces truck movements as estimated and maintains the jobs the grant is intended to support.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Westfield Quarry receives $680,000 freight rail grant
seoDescription: MassDOT awarded $680,000 to expand freight rail access at Westfield Quarry, with projected truck-trip reductions and 21 retained jobs.
